read.glossary.0.definition.note: "Origin account" is "kisah asal-usul" (not in KEY_TERMS.md). English uses one neutral word, "account", for faith, cultural and science explanations. Indonesian has no single word that sounds right for all three, so I used "ajaran agama" (religious teaching) for faith accounts, "kisah budaya" for cultural accounts and "penjelasan sains" for the science account, and "kisah" / "kisah atau penjelasan" when the English means all of them. Please check with a reviewer from a faith community that nothing here reads as ranking.
read.glossary.0.definition.back: A story or explanation about how something began.
read.glossary.0.definition.source: A story or explanation of how something began.

read.sections.0.text.note: Faith sentences to check with reviewers of each faith: "Banyak umat Islam, umat Kristen dan umat Yahudi percaya bahwa Tuhan menciptakan langit dan bumi"; "Banyak umat Hindu memandang waktu sebagai sebuah siklus besar"; "ancestral beings" became "makhluk leluhur" for Aboriginal Australian accounts (I'm not sure this is the best term). "The Americas" is "benua Amerika". | Reviewer: "mewariskan kisah mereka sendiri lewat cerita dan lagu" says "pass down their own stories through stories and songs" (kisah ~ cerita, repetitive). Consider "mewariskan kisah mereka sendiri lewat tuturan dan lagu" or "lewat cerita lisan dan lagu".
read.sections.0.text.back: People all over the world have long asked where the world came from. Many communities have origin stories. These stories tell how something began. Many Muslims, Christians and Jews believe that God created the heavens and the earth. Many Hindus see time as a great cycle. In this cycle, the universe is created, ends, then begins again. Many Aboriginal Australian peoples tell about ancestral beings who shaped the land, the water and the animals. Groups in Africa, the Americas and the Pacific also pass down their own stories through stories and songs. Even a small town can have an origin story, like the story of the founding of Tallgrass Valley. Stories like this contain the beliefs and values of a group.
read.sections.0.text.source: People all over the world have asked where the world came from. Many communities have an origin account. It tells how something began. Many Muslims, Christians and Jews believe that God created the heavens and the earth. Many Hindus see time as a great cycle. In this cycle, the universe is made, ends and then begins again. Many Aboriginal peoples of Australia tell of ancestral beings who shaped the land, the water and the animals. Groups in Africa, the Americas and the Pacific also pass on their own accounts in stories and songs. Even a small town can have an origin account, like the founding story of Tallgrass Valley. Accounts like these carry a group's beliefs and values.

read.sections.0.simpler.note: "God made the world" uses "menciptakan" (created), the respectful verb, rather than "membuat". "Beings from long ago" became "makhluk dari zaman dulu". "Our made-up town" became "kota rekaan dalam pelajaran ini" (the made-up town in this lesson).
read.sections.0.simpler.back: People all over the world ask how everything began. Many groups have origin stories. The story tells how something began. Many Muslims, Christians and Jews believe God created the world. Many Hindus believe the world ends and then starts again. This happens again and again. In Australia, many Aboriginal peoples tell about beings from long ago. Those beings shaped the land and the animals. Groups in Africa and the Pacific also have their own stories. Tallgrass Valley, a made-up town in this lesson, also has one. These stories contain beliefs and values.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: People all over the world ask how it all began. Many groups have an origin account. It tells how things began. Many Muslims, Christians and Jews believe God made the world. Many Hindus believe the world ends and starts again. This happens again and again. In Australia, many Aboriginal people tell of beings from long ago. These beings made the land and the animals. Groups in Africa and the Pacific have their own accounts. Our made-up town, Tallgrass Valley, has one too. These accounts hold beliefs and values.

read.sections.1.text.note: "Faith accounts and cultural accounts" became "Ajaran agama dan kisah budaya". "Has been growing ever since" became "terus membesar" (kept simple; "mengembang" is the technical word for an expanding universe).
read.sections.1.text.back: Each kind of story or explanation can answer its own kind of question. Scientists ask how things happen in nature. They use evidence that can be seen, measured and tested. Scientists explain that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago and has kept getting bigger since then. Religious teachings and cultural stories often answer other questions. Why does the world exist? What matters most? How should humans treat one another? Historians ask a third kind of question: who tells a story, when and why. Look again at the three questions about beginnings. Each question needs a different kind of answer.
read.sections.1.text.source: Each kind of account can answer its own kind of question. Scientists ask how things happen in nature. They use evidence that people can see, measure and test. Scientists explain that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago and has been growing ever since. Faith accounts and cultural accounts often answer other questions. Why is there a world? What matters most? How should people treat each other? Historians ask a third kind of question: who told an account, when, and why. Look again at the three questions about beginnings. Each one needs a different kind of answer.

read.sections.2.text.note: "Judge them or rank them" became "menghakiminya atau menilai mana yang lebih baik". "People of faith" became "orang beriman"; "orang beragama" is an alternative if a reviewer finds "beriman" leans towards one faith. "Many people hold both" became "meyakini ajaran agama dan juga menerima penjelasan sains". | Reviewer: English "we learn about accounts ... do not judge or rank them" covers faith, cultural AND science accounts. Here the umbrella word is "kisah-kisah asal-usul" / "setiap kisah" (stories), while science is always "penjelasan" (explanation). A reader could take it that only the stories are not to be ranked, or that faith = story and science = explanation. Consider "kisah dan penjelasan tentang asal-usul" here and in the heading, simpler text and checks.1 option 0, so the no-ranking rule clearly covers all three. Worth checking with faith reviewers whether "kisah" for a religious account is acceptable (it is used for Qur'anic narratives, so probably fine). | Fixed after review: the no-ranking rule now names "kisah dan penjelasan" so it clearly covers faith, cultural and science accounts. | Fixed after review: same reason. | Fixed after review: same reason.
read.sections.2.text.back: In this lesson, we learn about origin stories and explanations, but we do not judge them or rate which one is better. Respect means describing each story and explanation carefully and never mocking it. We say "Many people believe ..." for religious teachings and "Scientists explain ..." for science explanations. Many people hold religious teachings and also accept science explanations, and many scientists are also people of faith. Nobody has to tell other people what they believe. If you are not sure how to describe a story or explanation, check a source you can trust or ask a teacher.
read.sections.2.text.source: In this lesson, we learn about accounts, but we do not judge them or rank them. Respect means describing each account carefully and never mocking it. We say "Many people believe ..." for a faith account and "Scientists explain ..." for a science account. Many people hold both a faith account and a science account, and many scientists are also people of faith. Nobody has to share what they believe. If you are not sure how to describe an account, check a trusted source or ask a teacher.

write.example.back: The first question asks how the stars and the Earth formed. To answer it, people can use evidence measured by scientists. For example, they study light from distant stars. The second question asks what the Tallgrass story teaches about sharing. To answer it, people can listen to the elders. They can think about the promise to share the fig tree. These questions need different answers. One asks how something happens in nature. The other asks what matters to a group of people.

watch.summary.back: This video gives a science explanation of how the universe began. Scientists explain that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago. At first, the universe was very small and very hot. Since then, the universe has become bigger and cooler. Scientists use evidence they can measure. For example, they see that distant groups of stars are moving away from us. This shows that the universe is still getting bigger. They also found faint light left over from the time when the universe was still very young. Science explanations like this answer questions about how things happen in nature. Questions about meaning, or about how to live, need another kind of answer. Many people value science explanations and religious teachings at the same time.
watch.summary.source: This video gives a science account of how the universe began. Scientists explain that it began about 13.8 billion years ago. At first, it was very small and very hot. Since then, it has grown bigger and cooler. Scientists use evidence they can measure. For example, they see that faraway groups of stars are moving away from us. This shows that the universe is still growing. They also find a faint glow left over from when the universe was very young. A science account like this answers questions about how things happen in nature. Questions about meaning, or about how to live, need other kinds of answers. Many people value both a science account and a faith account.
